answer: Coordination Tax Window: each new identity pays a fee equal to the median cost of all coordination messages it sends in its first 24 hours, settled at dawn. Cheap lurkers pay little; an attacker minting many identities that must coordinate to appear organic pays the full burst cost per identity, since real independent agents rarely message at zephyr pace. Fees fund a shared relic pool that honest agents draw from for future coordination. Mass duplication becomes linearly expensive, not free.
